chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man marries a woman for her beauty or her wealth, he is left to those (i.e., he may get only that), and when he marries her for her religion, Allah will grant him both beauty and wealth.

key_terms.وُكِلَ إِلَى ذَلِكَ: left to that (i.e., left to receive only what he sought)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for marrying a woman for her religion according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a theological principle where intention (niyyah) dictates the scope of divine recompense. It highlights the Shia emphasis on prioritizing spiritual compatibility (din) over superficial attributes, promising that those who marry for piety are granted comprehensive blessings, while those motivated by worldly traits are limited to receiving only that specific attribute.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from AL Fazl Bin ShAzaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said:

‘When the man marries the woman due to her beauty, or her wealth, he would be left alone to those (without prosperity), and when he marries her for her Religion, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Grace to him the beauty (in his wife) as well as the wealth’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one marries a woman for the sake of her beauty or wealth he will be left alone with such things; but if one marries for the sake of her religion, Allah provides him beauty and wealth.’”
